title: Renewal concierge action plan — high-touch accounts
summary: Practical, tactical playbook for renewal risk assessment and rapid-response saves for high-touch enterprise accounts. Includes QBR-friendly templates, an escalation timeline, messaging scripts, and a short checklist for handoffs to execs and solutions engineering.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for the "renewal concierge" — CS managers + AMs assigned to high-touch accounts where renewal risk is unclear or rising. Focus: short, executable actions that surface root causes, contain churn, and escalate to the right partner (SE, solutions, legal, exec sponsor) quickly.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to: enterprise and strategic accounts (annual contract > $75k ARR, multi-product, or embedded infra customers)
- Owners: CSM (primary), AM (commercial lead), Solutions Eng (technical remediation), Customer Success Manager (renewal coordinator)
- Intended use: triage before QBR + tactical save plays in the 90 / 60 / 30 day renewal windows

Quick signals that trigger this playbook (use as checklist):
- Usage drop > 30% month-over-month for core product route
- Multiple unresolved P1/P2 incidents in last 60 days
- Support CSAT NPS decline > 10 points from baseline
- Executive sponsor change or silent sponsor (no active comms in 45 days)
- Billing disputes or procurement delays noted in tickets
- Public social posts or competitor procurement activity observed

Account health scoring (simple, actionable):
- Score components (0-100): Product usage (40%), Reliability/incidents (25%), Customer sentiment (20%), Commercial signals (15%)
- Buckets:
  - Green (>=80): Normal QBR cadence, no immediate action
  - Yellow (60–79): Preemptive outreach, schedule technical review, prep canary save play
  - Red (<60): Immediate escalation and 7-day remediation plan, notify execs

One-page QBR template (use in slides + notes):
- Slide 1: Executive summary (3 bullets: current state, risk level, immediate ask)
- Slide 2: Usage & business impact (top 2 KPIs, trends last 90 days)
- Slide 3: Reliability & ops (incidents, MTTR, mitigation deployed)
- Slide 4: Product roadmap sync (items that matter to customer)
- Slide 5: Proposed remediation / save plan (owner, ETA, dependencies, cost)
- Slide 6: Decision & next steps (renewal ask, support needed from execs)

Tiered save plays (fastest to heavier interventions):
- Tier A (light touch, <7 days): account health email + prioritized triage call, temporary free credits or usage extension, immediate SE deep-dive
- Tier B (medium, 7–21 days): targeted performance tuning, on-site workshop or dedicated SRE rotation, co-owned success plan with weekly checkpoints
- Tier C (heavy, >21 days): commercial concession (one-time invoice credit), product roadmap commitment with milestone SLAs, exec sponsorship pairing and public success plan

Immediate 7-day red response template (checklist):
1) Day 0: Alert exec sponsor + CS leadership (tagging protocol below). Create a shared war room doc and Slack channel.
2) Day 1: Triage call: CSM + AM + SE + SRE (60 min). Capture root cause hypotheses and immediate mitigations.
3) Day 2–3: Implement hotfixes / configuration changes; SE confirmation of impact.
4) Day 4: Customer-facing status update and draft QBR slide deck (use one-page template).
5) Day 5–7: Exec check-in with sponsor; confirm decision path for renewal (yes / extend / require concession).

Escalation matrix (who to call, and when):
- CSM: immediate owner for comms (always in the loop)
- AM: engaged when commercial language or contract/payment issues exist (within 24h of identifying risk)
- Solutions Eng: required for technical regressions impacting core SLA (24h)
- SRE/Infra Eng: if incident affects production or security (immediate)
- Legal/Finance: contacted if contract terms or billing disputes are present (48–72h)
- VP/Head of CS: notified for any Red account or if requires commercial concessions (within 48h)
- CRO / GM: only for high-dollar concessions or exec-level relationship repairs (ASAP, often day 3–5)

Slack tags & channel naming (operationalized):
- Use #warroom-<short-acct> for ephemeral channels. Prepend with [renewal] in channel topic.
- Tagging convention: @cs-lead, @am-<rep>, @se-oncall, @vp-cs for fast visibility

Messaging scripts (short):
- Initial outreach (CSM -> Sponsor):
  Subject: Quick check-in and plan to support [Customer] ahead of renewal
  Body: "Hi [Sponsor], I wanted to share a quick update on usage and a few items we think will help stabilize value ahead of renewal. Can we do a 30‑minute call this week to align on a short remediation plan? Our goal is to ensure you get full value before renew — we already have SEs on standby to implement quick fixes. — [CSM name]"

- Exec escalation email (to exec sponsor & internal exec):
  Subject: Red account alert — [Customer] — immediate remediation plan proposed
  Body: "TL;DR: [Customer] trending down in usage and reported multiple incidents; propose 7-day action with SE+SRE + potential one-time credit. Suggest VP/GM join daily stand for 5 days. Attached: one-page QBR."

Playbook for technical remediation (cheat-sheet for SEs):
- Snapshot current model: model/endpoint names, sequence length / prompt patterns, latency percentiles, KV cache hit rates, recent model changes or quantization profiles applied
- Rapid experiments: rollback recent model change -> measure 24h delta; test smaller context windows; increase batching limits only in non-prod to check stability
- If regression tied to infra: collect logs, request core dump / traces, and open SRE incident bridge

Commercial save tactics (negotiation playbook):
- Offer structure: time-limited credits tied to milestone delivery (e.g., 30% credit if MTTR drops below X and usage returns to baseline in 60 days)
- Avoid up-front percent-of-contract discounts without correlated technical plan and signed SLA acceptance
- If concession required, ensure CRO or finance pre-approves floor and document in amendment

Handoff checklist for Execs brought into the loop:
- One-page QBR + one-line ask (what we need from exec: time, introduction, concession approval)
- Risk score and three facts that matter to the customer (usage trend, top incident, roadmap mismatch)
- 2-minute briefing for exec (recorded) and preferred availability windows

Retention play log (use for handoffs and audit):
- Date | Owner | Action | Outcome | Next step (example row):
- 2026-02-01 | Maya Patel | Opened warroom, SE deep-dive scheduled | Found model overload causing latency | Applied throughput caps, monitor 72h

Open questions / notes to self:
- How quickly can Solutions commit to a dedicated SRE rotation (capacity constraints)? -> Ask infra leadership: JIRA INFRA-452
- Should we standardize a maximum one-time credit threshold per account tier? (finance / CRO input required)
- Can we add an automated signal in Console to tag accounts with usage drop + incidents -> triggers this doc creation? (linked artifact idea: product-ops ticket POR-27)

Appendix: quick references
- Template Slack message for war room creation (copy/paste)
- QBR slide template (link to slide deck stub)
- Example saved email archive (redacted)

Next steps (owner + due dates):
- Finalize 1-page QBR template (owner: Maya) — due 2025-12-05
- Run a dry-run escalation with 2 accounts this quarter (owner: Liam) — schedule by 2026-01-10
- Get finance threshold approved for one-time credits (owner: Sofia) — POC by 2026-01-20

Status / meta: this is a working doc — expect it to change after 2 field tests. Add comments inline and tag @Maya when you add new case notes.

----
Notes: kept intentionally conversational to make it usable during fast triage. If this migrates to Confluence, split checklist vs. templates into separate pages.
